v1.feedback: The leaf geometry is broken — `indices.push(i, i+1, i)` creates degenerate zero-area triangles, so the foliage meshes render as invisible; what remains on screen is just 1800 additive-blended point particles drifting through fog, which reads as a noise cloud. The CLIMATE_GLYPHS array is never rendered as actual text — the shader just uses glyphID to tint circular `gl_PointSize` dots, so the 'data stream' concept is invisible to the viewer. Fix the leaf geometry to be an actual surface (e.g., build a proper quad strip with width across the midrib), and either render the glyphs as real text sprites or drop them entirely — the climate-data theme feels bolted on and doesn't serve the 'plot-twist color swerve' idea, which is the one genuinely promising element here.

v2.feedback: The green-to-amber seasonal swerve is a legit plot-twist reading and the leaf meshes are properly constructed geometry (not noise), but the twist repeating on a fixed ~12s sine cycle turns 'surprise' into 'pulse' — consider making the first swerve delayed (20-30s) and subsequent ones aperiodic or escalating so the viewer is genuinely caught off guard. The 80k additive-blended particles risk washing the leaf silhouettes into a glow halo at certain angles; either tighten the particle ellipsoid radii closer to the mesh surfaces or drop to normal blending with a lower alpha floor so the quad-strip leaf geometry stays readable as the hero element.
